## RUN 1 — RED: the new tests against the base production file
$ cd .engine/stas-389-engine/packages/pi-claude-cli
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 × src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > a tool result cannot write the frame it is delivered in (AC2) > cannot terminate its own envelope, because on 2026-11-05 a payload holding the closing tag twice and the opening tag once turned one authored close tag into three and put the text after it outside any frame
 × src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > a tool result cannot write the frame it is delivered in (AC2) > cannot extend the frame either, because an opening tag the payload writes is a second envelope the assembler never authored and a reader cannot tell which one is real
 × src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > a tool result cannot write the frame it is delivered in (AC2) > still reaches the model byte-for-byte once the documented escaping is undone, because neutralising a delimiter must not quietly edit the report a tool actually printed
 × src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > a tool result cannot write the frame it is delivered in (AC2) > survives the ordinary case of a tool reading this very guard back, because the guard's own source contains these literals and refusing that output would break a routine read for every agent on this provider
 × src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > a tool result cannot mint a role key (AC1) > cannot produce a line-initial USER: the model could read as a new user turn, because the assembled string is handed over as the text of one user message and the only thing separating roles from data is that the assembler writes these keys
 × src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > a tool result cannot mint a role key (AC1) > cannot produce a line-initial ASSISTANT: either, because a forged assistant turn is how a payload gets its own words attributed to the assistant
 × src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > a tool result cannot mint a role key (AC1) > cannot mint the section key the assembler also emits, because `TOOL RESULT (<name>):` is a third key and not only the two the report named
 × src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > a tool result cannot mint a role key (AC1) > cannot mint a role key on the resumed-session delta, because that is where a fresh bash payload actually reaches the model and there the forged key was the only line-initial one besides the tool section
 ✓ src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > a tool result cannot mint a role key (AC1) > keeps a role word that merely appears inside a sentence untouched, because prose about a role is data and rewriting it would be the sledgehammer this card forbids
 ✓ src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > an ordinary payload is not rewritten (the anti-sledgehammer guard) > reaches the model byte-for-byte when it carries neither a frame delimiter nor a line-initial role key, because every payload the landed tests already pin must keep passing unchanged
 ✓ src/__tests__/tool-channel-authority.test.ts > an ordinary payload is not rewritten (the anti-sledgehammer guard) > keeps the empty payload saying so instead of going silent, because this card must not widen or weaken the fail-loud rule it builds on
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  8 failed | 3 passed (11)

  failing assertions, verbatim (these are the defect, not a paraphrase):
     → expected 2 to be 1 // Object.is equality
     → expected 3 to be 1 // Object.is equality
     → expected [ 'USER:', 'ASSISTANT:', …(2) ] to deeply equal [ 'USER:', 'ASSISTANT:', …(1) ]
     → expected [ 'TOOL RESULT (Bash):', 'USER:' ] to deeply equal [ 'TOOL RESULT (Bash):' ]

  Which names flipped is the pairing; the names still green in the RED run are
  green at BOTH revisions by design — they are the anti-sledgehammer guards, and a
  guard that went red at base would prove the transform rewrites payloads it must
  not touch. Their names are listed above with the failures so the pairing is not
  overstated.
